summary: Briar lookout in Ripley County, Missouri: a 100-foot steel tower built by a CCC camp (1936 or 1938), still standing, with no dedicated staff and restoration under way.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower, built with a towerman dwelling and two garages
facts.agency: Mark Twain National Forest, Eleven Point Ranger District

staffing.status: no dedicated staff; occasional fire-staff visits during fire season

events.note: Register: built by CCC Camp 3751 with a towerman dwelling and two garages. Forest Lookouts gives 1936 for the steel tower (see resolved_conflicts).
Lookout-dispatcher transferred to Briar Lookout Station on the Doniphan District
Local newspaper engagement notice says the man was presently employed at the Briar tower
Register: staffed frequently by employees until 2005; afterwards used for afternoon checks and locating reported smokes
Vandalism destroyed the Osborne fire finder; the Register dates this between 2005 and 2010
Restoration begun by a few district employees and AmeriCorps crews after years of disrepair
Fire finder stand damaged beyond repair by vandalism, then rebuilt and interior lower walls and floor repainted
Fire finder from the removed Fort Leonard Wood lookout gifted to the Forest, restored and placed in the lookout

evidence.supports: built by CCC Camp 3751 in 1938, with a towerman dwelling and two garages
evidence.quote: Constructed by Bardley CCC Camp 3751 in 1938 along with towerman dwelling (plan B34-01) and two garages (plan B-16).

evidence.supports: 1946 lookout-dispatcher transfer to the Briar station
evidence.quote: In his new position Martin will be located at Briar Lookout Station on the Doniphan District as Lookout-Dispatcher.

evidence.supports: 1965 item: a man presently employed at the Briar tower
evidence.quote: He is a graduate of Ellsinore High School and is presently employed at the Briar fire lookout tower.
Lookout was staffed frequently by employees until 2005.

evidence.supports: afternoon checks and smoke location after 2005
evidence.quote: After that time lookout was used for afternoon checks and locating reported smokes.

evidence.supports: vandalism destroyed the Osborne fire finder; disrepair until 2016
evidence.quote: Lookout was used infrequently after vandalism destroyed the Osborne fire finder between 2005 and 2010.

evidence.supports: disrepair until 2016 and restoration begun by employees and AmeriCorps
evidence.quote: Lookout was in disrepair until 2016 when efforts of a few district employees and AmeriCorps crews initiated restoration activities.

evidence.supports: 2021 fire finder stand damaged beyond repair by vandalism
evidence.quote: Lookout fire finder stand was damaged beyond repair by vandalism in 2021.

evidence.supports: stand rebuilt; interior lower walls and floor repainted
evidence.quote: Lookout stand was rebuilt and interior lower walls and floor repainted.

evidence.supports: 2024 fire finder from Fort Leonard Wood lookout restored and placed; tower standing
evidence.quote: The fire finder from the recently removed Fort Leonard Wood Lookout was gifted to the Forest, restored and placed in the lookout in 2024.

evidence.supports: no dedicated staff; prescribed fire monitoring and occasional fire staff visits
evidence.quote: Lookout does not have dedicated staff but is still utilized for prescribed fire monitoring as well as occasional visits from fire staff during fire season.

evidence.supports: administered by Mark Twain National Forest, Eleven Point Ranger District
evidence.quote: Mark Twain National Forest, Eleven Point Ranger District

evidence.supports: restoration ongoing: radio repeater, electric power, planned stair landings
evidence.quote: Restoration activities are ongoing including the addition of a radio repeater on the structure, restoration of electric power, planned replacement of all stairway landings with grated metal

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register dates construction to 1938 (CCC Camp 3751). The Forest Lookouts page gives 1936 for the steel tower's erection. The record keeps 1938 from the Register and the story reports both years.
A 1946 item places the station on the Doniphan District; the Register now names the Eleven Point Ranger District. The story uses the current name from the Register.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only: the Register and the Forest Lookouts page. The year conflict (1936 vs 1938) and the older district name are reported, not settled. Access is left out because neither source says whether visitors may climb it, and the schema has no unknown value. The staffing as_of date is the Register's registration date, not a dated staffing check. Brief values confirmed: 1938 build, 30.5 m (100 ft), agency, and the June 28, 2026 registration. The Register has a photo caption but no image URL, so no photo was added. Living New Deal returned 403 and was not used; an Instagram post and the Forest Service history page had nothing usable.
